double-check.example: The rubric asked students to double-check every quotation against the original page.
double-check.basic: The marking guide asked students to check every quotation a second time.

footnote.simple: A small note at the bottom of a page that adds extra information or a source.
footnote.detailed: A numbered or symbolled remark placed at the foot of a page to cite a source, define a term, or add a comment without breaking the main sentence.
footnote.example: A footnote on page 3 named the CSIRO report behind the salinity graph.
footnote.basic: A small note at the bottom of page 3 named the CSIRO report.

index.simple: An alphabetical list at the back of a book that shows on which pages topics appear.
index.detailed: A back-of-book finding aid that lists names and subjects with page numbers so a reader can locate information without scanning every chapter.
index.example: She used the index to jump straight to 'irrigation' instead of flipping every chapter.
index.basic: She used the alphabetical list at the back to jump straight to 'irrigation'.

keyword.simple: An important word you search for, or that captures the main idea of a text.
keyword.detailed: A term that unlocks a search, catalogue, or argument because it names a central concept; also used for the words a reader highlights as essential.
keyword.example: Using the keyword 'catchment' found better science pages than searching 'water place'.
keyword.basic: Using the important search word 'catchment' found better science pages.

margin.simple: The blank space around the edge of a page, used for notes or to keep text readable.
margin.detailed: The unprinted border of a page or screen; in schoolwork it is where annotations, corrections, and teacher comments often sit.
margin.example: Leave a wide margin on the left so the marker can write next to each paragraph.
margin.basic: Leave a wide blank edge on the left so the marker can write comments.

paragraph.simple: A group of sentences about one idea, starting on a new line.
paragraph.detailed: A unit of prose that develops a single point or step, usually marked by a break or indent, and built around a topic sentence.
paragraph.example: The second paragraph explained the method, so the results table made sense.
paragraph.basic: The second block of sentences explained the method.

quotation.simple: The exact words copied from a speaker or a text, usually shown inside inverted commas.
quotation.detailed: A precise extract reproduced from another source, set off by punctuation or layout and normally accompanied by a reference.
quotation.example: A long quotation needs a page number; otherwise the marker cannot check it.
quotation.basic: A long copied sentence needs a page number so the marker can check it.

reference.simple: A note that shows where a piece of information came from.
reference.detailed: A citation of a book, article, website, or person that lets a reader find the original source; also the act of pointing to that source.
reference.example: Every graph in the report needed a reference so the marker knew which bureau supplied the data.
reference.basic: Every graph needed a source note so the marker knew who supplied the data.

rubric.simple: A marking guide that shows how a piece of work will be scored.
rubric.detailed: A published set of criteria and grade descriptions that tells students what quality looks like at each level of a task.
rubric.example: According to the rubric, a Level 5 answer had to use two sources, not just one website.
rubric.basic: According to the marking guide, a top answer had to use two sources.

skimming.simple: Reading quickly to get the main idea, not every word.
skimming.detailed: A reading strategy that sweeps headings, first sentences, and key nouns to decide what a text is about before a slower, closer read.
skimming.example: Skimming the introduction told Oliver the article was about salinity, so he slowed down at the data.
skimming.basic: Reading the introduction quickly told Oliver the article was about salinity.

subheading.simple: A smaller heading that splits a text into labelled parts.
subheading.detailed: A secondary title under a main heading that signals the topic of the next section and helps a reader scan the structure.
subheading.example: The subheading 'Method' saved her from mixing the equipment list into the conclusion.
subheading.basic: The smaller heading 'Method' saved her from mixing the equipment list into the conclusion.

timeline.simple: A line that shows events in the order they happened, often with dates.
timeline.detailed: A graphic or list that places events along a chronological scale so causes, overlaps, and gaps in time become visible.
timeline.example: The Federation timeline showed the referendums before 1901, not just the opening of parliament.
timeline.basic: The dated event line showed the referendums before 1901.

wording.simple: The exact words someone chooses, which can change the tone or meaning.
wording.detailed: The particular phrasing of a sentence or question; small changes in the chosen words can make a claim fairer, vaguer, or more precise.
wording.example: Changing the wording from 'kids dumped rubbish' to 'litter increased' made the claim easier to support.
wording.basic: Changing the exact words from 'kids dumped rubbish' to 'litter increased' made the claim easier to support.

coastline.simple: The edge where land meets the sea, including bays, cliffs, and beaches.
coastline.detailed: The boundary between terrestrial and marine environments, shaped by waves, tides, and geology, and often mapped for planning and conservation.
coastline.example: Erosion had cut the coastline back so the old fence now stood in the high-tide zone.
coastline.basic: Waves had cut the land's sea-edge back so the old fence stood in the high-tide zone.

drought.simple: A long period with far less rain than usual, so land, rivers, and farms dry out.
drought.detailed: A prolonged shortage of precipitation relative to the local average, causing low soil moisture, stressed ecosystems, and hardship for communities.
drought.example: During the drought the dam fell so low that the old bridge piles stood in air.
drought.basic: During the long dry period the dam fell so low that the old bridge piles stood in air.

floodplain.simple: Flat land beside a river that floods when the river overflows.
floodplain.detailed: A low, relatively level area adjacent to a channel, built of sediment from past overflows and still liable to inundation in high flow.
floodplain.example: Houses on the floodplain had to be built on stilts after the 2022 floods.
floodplain.basic: Houses on the flat land beside the river had to be built on stilts.

headland.simple: A high piece of land that juts out into the sea.
headland.detailed: A coastal promontory of resistant rock that projects into the ocean, often with cliffs, and that helps shape nearby bays.
headland.example: From the headland they could see both the sheltered bay and the open swell.
headland.basic: From the high point of land they could see both the sheltered bay and the open swell.
